notes: Maedhros' hill-fortress that held the Leaguer's east — and held after the Bragollach.

“Himling was the earlier form of Himring (the great hill on which Maedhros son of Feanor had his fortress in The Silmarillion), and though the fact is nowhere referred to it is clear that Himring's top rose above the waters that covered drowned Beleriand.” — Unfinished Tales, Christopher Tolkien's note [I-H — his inference, and he says so: 'the fact is nowhere referred to']
the hill's top remained as the isle of Himling, drawn on Tolkien's own sketch-map and on Christopher Tolkien's first draft map
drawn on the vector spec's FA plate, which its Section 0 calls First Age Beleriand
the vector spec also lists it as “Himring citadel”, at the same place; one record, not two
the inferred drowning of Beleriand is not carried here: the corpus says this place remained

timeline.what: After Thingol's word, the sons of Fëanor remove east; Maedhros holds Himring
The Bragollach: Himring alone stands; the Gap and Lothlann lost
